fields.name: plan_subunit_difference
fields.comment: Per CSubUnitDefinition::type_index: what the plan wants of that type minus what the unit's OOB actually has. Signed - a negative entry is a surplus. Written wholesale by CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds (0x1BD240) and cleared by CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds for an HQ that has no plan. (reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_subunit_group_difference
fields.comment: The same differences summed onto one representative subunit type per group (0x1ADF70 does the folding: carrier air, capital ship, transport/submarine, and so on). Zeroed at the top of each pass and accumulated at 0x1BD544. (reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_subunit_needed
fields.comment: Per subunit type, the part of the deficit that the group as a whole is still short of - min(difference[i], whatever is left of that group's net difference), taken in index order. This is the list the plan machinery asks for. (reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_active
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x8. Whether the unit's battle plan is switched on; CUnitPlan::SetActive (0x4DEB10) resets the whole plan when it goes to zero. (reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_stance
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0xC, the `stance` key. Defaults to 2 when the plan is switched off. The one plan attribute whose change makes CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute call CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds; 5 is the command's "not set" sentinel. (reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_air_stance
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x10, the `air_stance` key. 3 is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel for it. (reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_naval_stance
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x14, the `naval_stance` key. 3 is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel for it. (reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_subunit_wanted
fields.comment: The composition the plan asks for, per subunit type - the array 0x4E1D00 fills from the plan and the owner's available subunit types. Sits inside CUnit::plan at plan+0x70. (reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_our_power
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x80, the `our_power` key - the plan's cached estimate of the owner's strength for it. A negative value is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel. (reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_their_power
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x84, the `their_power` key - the plan's cached estimate of the opposition's strength. A negative value is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel. (reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

(reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.comment: which countries are in the Neighbours list at +0xFD8: a byte per country, indexed by its id. RebuildNeighbours (0xE21E0) walks the provinces this country **owns** and marks the owner of each adjacent province whose owner and controller are the same - so not one somebody is occupying - and which is neither unowned nor this country. fields.name: controller_neighbours
fields.comment: which countries are in the ControllerNeighbours list at +0xFE8, the same shape as neighbours. RebuildNeighbours walks the provinces this country **controls** and marks the controller of each adjacent province that is owned by somebody and neither owned nor controlled by this country. So occupation moves a country from one set to the other: Sweden has Denmark in neither, and Germany here, because Germany holds Denmark. CCountry::IsNonExileNeighbour reads this and then checks the other country is not a government in exile, which this list does not do for itself (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:357)

fields.name: in_game
fields.comment:
Nonzero while the in-game screen is the live one: set to 1 at `0x25D126`, the end of `CInGameIdler::Enter`'s session build, and cleared by `CInGameIdler::Leave` (`0x262337`), by `CFrontEnd`'s enter (`0x2EFE58`) and at `0x2ED9AF`. Zeroed by every construction of the game state.

**This is the attrition gate.** `CUnit::UpdateDaily` tests it at `DailyTickEndGate` (`0x1BB3E8`) and skips both `ApplyAttrition` and `CheckTransportOverload` when it is zero - so it is not a development-era "enable attrition" switch, and attrition does run. About twenty other places test it before touching live game data (`0x255AB7` reaches `strategic_warfare`, `0x4349B2` reaches the player tag), which is the sense the name is taken from: a game is running.

One byte. The last field of the class: the object is allocated `0xDA8` bytes and the constructor tail writes a word at `+0xD9C`, a dword at `+0xDA0` and this byte, so `+0xDA5..+0xDA7` are padding.

Not saved: no access to it lives in the save or load code, and no key in a `.hoi3` save corresponds to it.

**Confirmed in a running game**, not only traced: sampled every frame it read 0 at the main menu with the pointer already live, 1 once a campaign was up - while the clock was still not reporting in play, which is the write landing before the in-game GUI is built - and 0 again on returning to the menu. See `Reversing/Watch.hpp`. (reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

fields.name: current_experience
fields.comment: **one 64-bit value, not two words**: the loader reads `current_experience` with `%lld` into these eight bytes and CLeader::AddExperience adds to them with `add`/`adc` and compares them against the threshold as a pair. The game's 48.15 fixed point, and a career total rather than a per-level count. **The high half can be reached**: the skill-10 threshold is unreachable by design, so a leader parked there keeps accruing, passing 2^31 after another 5536 experience points. **Read live**: zero high halves on 8000 leaders and a largest total of 809977445, 38% of the way to 2^31 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CLeader.hpp:48)

fields.comment: **the skill the mod's files define**: the `skill` handler writes it here too but only while it is still negative, so it keeps the first value, and CLeader::ResetToStarting puts it back into `skill`. **Read live**: matching 7296 leaders to history/leaders/*.txt on country and id, it is the file's `skill` on every one of them - 6179 still at it, 1117 risen above it through experience, **none below it**. Nothing in the image decrements +0x70, and the only path that lowers it is ResetToStarting, which resets to the definition rather than below it (BiceLib/GameClasses/CLeader.hpp:81)

fields.name: starting_experience
fields.comment: the experience the leader was defined with, in whole points, saved as `experience`. CLeader::ResetToStarting scales it by 32768/1000 into `current_experience`. **Read live**: zero on all 8000 leaders (BiceLib/GameClasses/CLeader.hpp:82)

fields.name: type
fields.comment: the token's kind, itself a token id: 1 `=`, 3 `{`, 4 `}`, 0x10 a newline, 0x11 a tab, 0x12 a space, 0x13 the end of input, 0x14 an integer, 0x18F long_float. In a binary save this is what gets written, as two bytes. (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:76)

fields.comment: the key just read. Its type is the token id CPersistent::Load hands slot 4, which is what a class switches on. (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:104)

fields.name: separator
fields.comment: the `=` between the key and the value (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:105)

fields.name: value

fields.name: messages_first
fields.comment: First node of the parse messages list; a node is two Hoi3CStrings at +0 and +0x20 with the next pointer at +0x40. CParseContext::FreeMessages is handed this field's address - the destructor passes `this+4` - and frees the chain. (reversing/FINDINGS-redeploy.md)

fields.name: messages_last
fields.comment: Last node of the parse messages list; cleared with the other two when the list is freed. (reversing/FINDINGS-redeploy.md)

fields.name: messages_count
fields.comment: How many messages are in the list; cleared when it is freed. Nothing reads it on the way out, which is why a file full of unknown keys is silent. (reversing/FINDINGS-redeploy.md)

fields.name: session_name
fields.comment: The name the context was made with - the third argument of `CParseContext::CParseContext` (0x67A460), which takes it in EDX and assigns it here; the destructor (0x67A630) frees it with the usual `capacity >= 0x10` test, size at `+0x33C` and capacity at `+0x340`. Two constructor call sites pass the literal `UNNAMED_SESSION` (0x1002AF, 0x231700), which is where the name comes from. Exactly two places read it: `CCommand::LoadKey` (0x67BCD0) copies it into the command's own string at `+8` when that is still empty, and `ParseObjectReference` (0x1EC150) copies it into every object reference it fills. Nothing writes it after construction and neither copy is ever saved, so it is a runtime label for which stream a command or a reference came out of. **The `session` reading is inferred** from the default literal; what is checked is that it is a string and who its five users are. (reversing/FINDINGS-script.md)

fields.name: error_handler
fields.comment: Null in the ordinary constructor (0x67A460); set from the caller's EDI by the second one (0x67A520), whose six call sites are all in the 0xB3xxxx network module. `ReportParseError` (0x67A960) sets the byte at its `+4`, calls its slot 0 with the parse context and, where that returns true, sets `+5` as well and queues no message. `ParseObjectReference` (0x1EC150) reads the same three and stores nothing when all three are set, so once the handler has taken an error the block is still consumed but its value is dropped. project.json already describes `+4` in ReportParseError's comment; this names the field it hangs off. (reversing/FINDINGS-script.md)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57)

functions.name: operator=
functions.evidence:
Four instructions: `assign(source, 0, npos)`. **The source arrives in eax** - the compiler gave this thunk a convention of its own - and the destination in ecx as usual. Eight call sites. What CCountry::SetOobFile is made of.
(reversing/FINDINGS-effecttext.md)

functions.name: clear
functions.evidence:
Gives the buffer back where the string had one - `if (capacity >= 0x10) free(data)` - and leaves it empty: capacity 0xF, length 0, first byte 0. The destructor's body as well as `clear()`, which is why it turns up at the end of every function that built a string.
(reversing/FINDINGS-effecttext.md)

functions.name: assignString
functions.evidence:
**Replaces** this string with part of another - the same three arguments and the same bounds check as `appendString` (`0x33E30`), and the pair are easy to mistake for each other. **5489 call sites.** The requirement renderer uses this one to hand its finished text back through the out parameter.
(reversing/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: Get
functions.evidence:
Lua: CFixedPoint:Get   (script/LUA API.txt, CFixedPoint::Get)
Registered as: luabind::detail::memfun_registration<CFixedPoint,float (__thiscall CFixedPoint::*)(void)const ,luabind::detail::null_type>
luabind signature: float Get(CFixedPoint const&)
Recovered by emulating SetupAI (0x8EAE30): the registration object luabind builds for this def holds this address.

functions.name: clear
functions.evidence:
**`std::ios_base::clear(iostate, bool)`**, the bottom of every stream error path. `_Mystate` (`+0xC`) = `state & 0x17` (MSVC's `_Statmask`); if nothing in the new state is in `_Except` (`+0x10`) it returns; if `reraise` it rethrows with `_CxxThrowException(0, 0)`; otherwise it throws `std::ios_base::failure` carrying `ios_base::badbit set` (0x15B4E4C), `ios_base::failbit set` (0x15B4E64) or `ios_base::eofbit set` (0x15B4E7C), in that priority order, through `_CxxThrowException` with the `_ThrowInfo` at 0x164B158.

`this` is the `basic_ios` (== the `ios_base` subobject), so callers reach it as `[[os]+4] + os`. The `basic_ios::clear` wrapper is inlined at every call site as the two instructions `cmp dword ptr [ecx+0x38], 0 / or eax, 4` - the 'no rdbuf means badbit' rule - which is why the callee never looks at the buffer itself.
(reversing/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: endl
functions.evidence:
**`std::endl`** - MSVC's `basic_ostream<char>::put(widen('\n')); flush(); return os`, out of line. `__cdecl`, one stack argument, bare `ret`, answers the stream in eax so it chains.

The body is two halves. The `put('\n')` half is the call to `0x9B50`, which is `__stdcall` and cleans the argument itself - which is why there is no `add esp,4` after it at any call site. The `flush()` half is inlined here and is instruction for instruction the body of `std::ostream::flush` at `0x65BB20`: `if (!(rdstate() & (failbit|badbit)) && rdbuf()->pubsync() == -1) state = badbit;` then `if (state) clear(rdstate() | state | (rdbuf() ? 0 : badbit), false)` through `std::ios_base::clear` at `0x20B0`.

**681 direct call sites, and they are the game's log.** The idiom is `LogRecord::Make(file, line, channel) << "text" << ... << endl` - `0x2410` builds the record, `0xA64A00`/`0xA64A30` are its own inserters, `0x21D30` writes the C strings and this ends the line. `*::LoadKey` dominates the caller list because that is where the engine complains about a key it did not understand. MSVC inlined the same pair at about 120 further sites (`0x16E92` is one: `push esi; call 0x409B50` followed by a private copy of the flush body), so the real number of `<< endl` in this executable is higher than the call count.

The stream is reached through a virtual base: `[[os]+4] + os` is the `basic_ios`, whose fields this touches are `+0xC` `_Mystate` and `+0x38` `_Mystrbuf`.

functions.name: Make
functions.evidence:
**Builds one log record**, and first makes sure there is a sink: if `g_log_sink` (`0x17162A4`) is still null it allocates the four byte do-nothing sink whose vftable is `0x11FCEA0` and installs that, so a message logged before `InstallLogSink` is discarded rather than queued. Then calls the register-convention forwarder `LogRecord::Construct` (`0x6649D0`) with the file, the sink, the line and the channel. There is **no channel test here or anywhere after it** - every record built is flushed to the sink. `this` arrives in ECX and is returned in EAX; the three stack arguments are cleaned by the caller (bare `ret`, `add esp, 0xC` at the call site), so the convention is `__cdecl` with a register `this`, not `__thiscall`.

functions.name: Flush
functions.evidence:
**The complete destructor of the record, and where a log line is decided.** Every message in the game arrives here in a record holding its file, line and channel, and this is what does or does not write it - `[persistent.cpp:39]`, `[countryhistory.cpp:450]` and the 597KB of setup.log all pass through it. Nothing is returned: eax at the `ret` is whatever `~ios_base` left there and no caller reads it. **The one place worth hooking to see everything the engine complains about**, including the channels that produce no file.

functions.name: operator<<Chars
functions.evidence:
**`std::operator<<(std::ostream&, const char*)`** - the free inserter for a C string, out of line. `__cdecl`, `os` at `[ebp+8]`, the string at `[ebp+0xC]`, bare `ret`, answers `os` in eax. The `Chars` suffix distinguishes it from the other `operator<<` overloads, the way `std::string::appendChars` is distinguished from `appendString` in these findings.

It is the standard algorithm, in order: `strlen` inline (0x421D61, and the same inline `strlen` opens `std::string::assign`'s caller at 0x4022A0); `pad = width() > len ? width() - len : 0`, computed as a full 64-bit compare and subtract because `streamsize` is `__int64` here, against `_Wide` at basic_ios `+0x20`/`+0x24`; then the sentry - `rdbuf()->_Lock()`, and if `_Mystate == 0` and `_Tiestr` (`+0x3C`) is set, `_Tiestr->flush()` through 0xA5BB20; if the sentry is not ok, `badbit`. When it is ok, `(_Fmtfl & 0x1C0) == 0x40` - `adjustfield == left` - decides whether the padding goes after the text (0x421F44) or before it (0x421E22); the fill character is `_Fillch` at `+0x40` and each one goes out through the sputc fast path or `overflow`. The text itself goes through `sputn` (0x22170) and a short write is `badbit`. Then `width(0)` - `_Wide` zeroed at 0x421EA4 - `setstate(state)` through `std::ios_base::clear`, and the sentry's destructor: `uncaught_exception()` (0x794AE9), `_Osfx` (0xA260), `rdbuf()->_Unlock()`.

**845 direct call sites**, for the same reason as `std::endl`: this is what writes every literal in the game's log lines, and `*::LoadKey` is over-represented because that is where parse complaints are written.

basic_ios is a virtual base, reached as `[[os]+4] + os`; the fields used are `+0xC` `_Mystate`, `+0x14` `_Fmtfl`, `+0x20` `_Wide` (64 bit), `+0x38` `_Mystrbuf`, `+0x3C` `_Tiestr`, `+0x40` `_Fillch`.
(reversing/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: sputn
functions.evidence:
Seven instructions: hand `(text, count)` to the buffer's virtual at `+0x24` - slot 9, `xsputn` - and answer what it answers, a 64-bit count in edx:eax. `ret 0xC`, so `__thiscall` with a pointer and a `streamsize`. `std::operator<<Chars` compares the result against the length it asked for and sets `badbit` when they differ.

What this country pays for a building: the building's own cost (CBuilding +0x58) scaled by the discount its technology category earns, cost x (1000 - discount) / 1000. The slot 2 call on the category that guards it is the folded `mov al,1; ret` at 0xA92590, true for a real category and for the nocategory object alike, so the discount is always applied. That matters for a building whose category is nocategory - its index is 0, where every country's ability is 0, and an ability below 5.000 raises the cost: A building whose category is nocategory therefore costs about half as much again.

functions.name: LoadOobFile
functions.evidence:
**Reads the order of battle named at `CCountry::oob_file`** and puts it in the country. functions.name: Distribute
functions.evidence:
**Slot 0 of its virtual table, and where the manpower tooltip's two numbers come from.** The class derives from `CDistributionSetting`, so this is the reinforcement slider spending what it has been allocated; every sibling distributor - supply, upgrade, production, research, consumer goods, lend lease, NCO, diplomacy, espionage - has its own body at the same slot.

It zeroes `CCountry +0xA98`, `+0xA9C` and `+0xAA0`, then walks the country's units and every subunit under each, and rebuilds all three from nothing. `this + 0x18` is the country throughout.

**The stack arguments are three, not one**, which is why the recorded signature wanted ret 4 and the function does ret 16: a hidden return pointer at [ebp+8] for the eight-byte fixed point it answers, the amount it has been given as a 64-bit `fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15>` split across [ebp+0xC] and [ebp+0x10], and a byte flag at [ebp+0x14]. This body ignores the flag; the consumer-goods (0x118C50) and production (0x119D10) bodies read it and skip their last step when it is set. `__int64` is written for the middle argument only so the arithmetic sizes - it is the same fixed point type as the return.

functions.name: AddExperience

functions.name: MakeSubUnit
functions.evidence:
**Builds a throwaway regiment to compare models against.** From the set's definition it news a CRegiment, a ship or an air unit by the two flags at `CSubUnitDefinition +0x2C` and `+0x2E`, calls CSubUnit::SetType, then walks the definition's `technologies` vector (`+0x44..+0x48`) and writes each one's researched level - `CTechnologyStatus::level_by_technology[technology->index]` of the country the set's tag names - into the matching node of the new regiment's `technologies` list, and finishes with CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies. Its only caller destroys it immediately. The name is BiceLib's.
(BiceLib/GameClasses/CHistoricalModel.hpp)

functions.name: PickCurrentModel
functions.evidence:
**The model a country would build right now**: MakeSubUnit for a regiment carrying the country's current research, PickBestModel against it, then the regiment's deleting destructor. Takes its one argument in eax and answers in eax, an LTCG convention. The name is BiceLib's.
(BiceLib/GameClasses/CHistoricalModel.hpp)

functions.name: PickBestModel
functions.evidence:
**Which of a unit type's models a country would build today.** `ret 4`, so it takes **one** stack argument, not two: ecx is the CHistoricalModelSet whose first three words are the model vector, and the stack argument is a CSubUnit whose `technologies` list at `+0x84` says what the country has researched. It scores every model as the sum, over the model's own CSubUnitTechnology entries, of `|the regiment's level - the level the model wants| * 1000`, **counting only technologies whose `CTechnology::change` is set** (789 of 1175 in this mod), and answers the model with the smallest total - starting from 999,999,000, and null for an empty set. **The absolute value is what `Patches::historicalModelLogicFix` replaces**, so that a model asking for more than is researched is penalised rather than treated as equally close. The name is BiceLib's.
(BiceLib/GameClasses/CHistoricalModel.hpp)

functions.name: Find
functions.evidence:
The A* search itself, and **not a member call**: the finder is the first stack argument, not a receiver. The call site at rva 0x1D8F08 pushes five and adds nothing back (the body does `ret 0x14`), and ECX there holds the unit's own province from CUnit +0x130 - so nothing puts the finder in a register.

What it does: refuses unless unit, from and to are all non-null, then asks the finder's slot 1 (MayUse) whether it may run at all. It allocates three arrays the size of the game state's province vector - a visited byte per province, a 16-byte open-list record per province and a came-from index per province - and loops: take the cheapest open province, ask slot 3 (IsGoal), and for each edge of its template (CProvince +0xD4) ask slot 2 (MayStep) and then slot 0 (StepCost). The heuristic added on top is the straight-line distance between the two templates' +0x2C/+0x30 coordinates, wrapped at the map width in CMap +0x2A74 and scaled by [0x1688618]. On success rva 0x1A11F0 fills `path` with 16-byte nodes holding province **ids** (the CList head is first/last/count/flag, the nodes are data/prev/next/flag).
(reversing/FINDINGS-redeploy.md)

functions.name: MayUse
functions.evidence:
CPathFind slot 1: whether this finder may be used for this unit at all. CPathFind::Find asks it once, before allocating anything, and answers false when it does. `this` is not read - see CPathFind::StepCost for why the convention is still __thiscall - and `ret 0xC` covers the three stack arguments.

False unless the unit's own slot 34 (vftable +0x88) accepts `to`. If the unit's slot 16 (+0x40) then says nothing, true; if it does, the test at rva 0xA7D70 - `to` in ECX, `from` in EAX, `&unit->owner` pushed - has to agree as well.
(reversing/FINDINGS-redeploy.md)

functions.name: MayStep
functions.evidence:
CPathFind slot 2: whether `unit` may step from `from` to `to` along `edge`, with `goal` the search's destination (which the base ignores and both safe finders use). `this` is not read; `ret 0x14` covers the five stack arguments.

Refuses when the edge's kind is 3, when `from` is `to`, when `goal`'s template flag +0x13D is clear, and when the helper at rva 0x1A2600 says a kind-1 edge is blocked - that one reads the province the edge crosses (edge +8) and refuses if its controller is hostile or a foreign unit that is not retreating stands in it. Then the two provinces' templates have to agree: the byte at template **+0x22, unnamed**, may not be set on both, and where it is set on one, that template's **+0xA4, unnamed**, must be the other province's id. What follows is the supply gate: with the destination's controller hostile (rva 0x2F1B0) it refuses a unit whose supply_received_percentage is zero and whose CUnit::SupplyConsumption is positive, and likewise fuel_received_percentage against CUnit::FuelConsumption; and last, the unit owner's relation record for `from`'s controller (country +0xE28 indexed by tag id, byte **+0x4C unnamed**) together with **+0x20** on the record for `to`'s controller refuses the step.
(reversing/FINDINGS-redeploy.md)

functions.name: IsGoal
functions.evidence:
CPathFind slot 3, which no class in the family overrides: `sete` on `goal == at`, three stack arguments, `ret 0xC`, and neither `this` nor `unit` read. CPathFind::Find asks it for every province it takes off the open list and builds the path the moment it answers 1 (0x5A13B3-0x5A13B7), which is what the name says. Slot 3 was previously recorded only as "unknown" on the CPathFind vftable entry.
(reversing/FINDINGS-redeploy.md)

functions.name: StepCost
functions.evidence:
CPathFind slot 0: the cost of stepping out of `from` along its edge number `edge`. **The name is right and the receiver is in ECX.** The body belongs to CPathFind - vtable.py --holding puts it at slot 0 of CPathFind, CSafePathFind, CVerySafePathFind and CPlannedPathFind, which inherit it, while CSafeNavalPathFind overrides it at 0x1A2E00 - and CPathFind::Find loads ECX with the finder at every one of its four dispatch sites (0x1A12E5, 0x1A1390, 0x1A143A, 0x1A145C). The body never reads ECX because these finders are four-byte objects holding nothing but a vftable pointer; that is a `this` that is not needed, not a missing argument. `ret 0x14` accounts for the five stack arguments exactly.

The cost is `from->edges_begin[edge].distance`, in thousandths. Then, if the country controlling `map->provinces[from->edges_begin[edge].to_province]` is hostile to the unit's owner - the tag test at rva 0x2F1B0 - it is scaled by 1100/1000, or by 2000/1000 when that province's intel byte for the owner (CProvince +0x370, bounds-checked against +0x374) is 2 or more **and** units are standing in it (+0x2C0). The two constants are the floats at 0x160A5F0 (1100.5) and 0x160A5F4 (2000.5), truncated to int. Returns `out` in EAX, MSVC's struct return.
(reversing/FINDINGS-redeploy.md)

functions.name: MayStep
functions.evidence:
CSafePathFind slot 2. Forwards all five arguments unchanged to CPathFind::MayStep (0x5A2AFB-0x5A2B00, no ECX set, callee cleans) and refuses on top of it. Allows the step outright when `to` is the goal - the last step into the destination is exempt. Otherwise it weighs the destination: when the unit's slot 16 or 17 answers true it takes rva 0x1D6900 over `to`'s unit list with the unit's owner tag and multiplies by 1000; when neither does it walks that list itself and adds rva 0x1C3120's value for each unit there whose owner is hostile (rva 0x2F1B0), skipping a `REB` owner when the province's owner tag id (CProvince +0x330) is the unit's own. Either way it refuses when that total is greater than the sum of +0x5C over the unit's own list at CUnit +0xB8.

functions.name: MayStep
functions.evidence:
CVerySafePathFind slot 2, the same shape as CSafePathFind's: forwards all five arguments to CPathFind::MayStep (0x5A2C5B-0x5A2C60), exempts the last step into the goal, and refuses otherwise. functions.name: MayUse

functions.name: MayStep

functions.name: StepCost

functions.name: UpdatePlanForceNeeds
functions.evidence:
Recomputes, per subunit type, what this unit's order of battle is short of against its plan. The three vector<int> arguments are always &unit->+0x5C, &unit->+0x6C and &unit->+0x7C at both call sites; all three are indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index and sized to the subunit definition database's count ((db+0x20 - db+0x1C)/4), grown and zero-filled on the first call and, on later calls, with the second and third zeroed at 0x1BD40C while the first is overwritten wholesale. It then walks up higher_oob_unit_ptr to the top of the OOB and, unless that top unit has plan+0x8 (CUnit +0x204) set with oob_level 0, calls ComputePlanWantedSubUnits (0x4E1D00) to build the wanted composition out of the unit's plan (CUnit +0x1FC) and the owner's available subunit types; with the fifth argument null it fills the plan's own buffers at plan+0x18/+0x70/+0x80/+0x84, with it non-null it fills locals instead. The wanted list is the local one where 0x4E1D00 produced one and unit->+0x26C (which is plan+0x70) otherwise. CUnit::CountSubUnitsByType (0x1BD7E0) then counts what the unit actually has, and: difference[i] = wanted[i] - have[i]; groupDifference[GenericType(i)] += difference[i] for every non-zero entry, where GenericType is 0x1ADF70 folding a subunit type onto a representative one; then, over a copy of groupDifference, needed[i] = min(difference[i], groupNet) for each positive deficit, drawing that group's remaining net down as it goes - so a surplus of one type inside a group cancels a deficit of another.     if (this->fallback_line)   CUnitPlan::SetFallbackLine(plan, &this->provinces)   // plan +0x28, returns here
    else                       CUnitPlan::SetOpsArea(plan, &this->provinces)        // plan +0x18

                                       gamestate->+0xBE8 slot 32(...)               // 0x1E649F

functions.name: Execute
functions.evidence:
Slot 6 of `CSetPlanAttributesCommand` - the command's own **Execute** (see `CCommand::Execute`). It resolves the command's `unit` reference and writes the six battle-plan attributes it carries onto that unit's embedded `CUnitPlan` (`CUnit +0x1FC`), each with a sentinel meaning "not set by this command":

| command field | key | sentinel | lands on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `+0x64` byte | `active` | none | `CUnitPlan::SetActive` (`0x4DEB10`) |
| `+0x68` | `stance` | `== 5` skips | plan `+0xC` = `CUnit +0x208` |
| `+0x6C` | `air_stance` | `== 3` skips | plan `+0x10` = `CUnit +0x20C` |
| `+0x70` | `naval_stance` | `== 3` skips | plan `+0x14` = `CUnit +0x210` |
| `+0x74` | `our_power` | `< 0` skips | plan `+0x80` = `CUnit +0x27C` |
| `+0x78` | `their_power` | `< 0` skips | plan `+0x84` = `CUnit +0x280` |

Only the `stance` branch calls `CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds` (at `0x1E78B4`) - changing the ground stance is what changes what the plan needs; the air and naval stances and the two power estimates do not.

**It re-resolves the unit for every field it writes** - six separate `FindPersistentById` lookups off `this->+0x40`/`+0x44` - rather than resolving once, which is why the body is four times longer than what it does. Each lookup has a failure arm that falls through to `xor eax, eax` and then stores through the null pointer anyway (`0x1E79EB` writes `[0 + 0x280]`); the game survives only because a command whose target has gone is rejected by `IsValid` before slot 6 is reached.
(reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

functions.name: Execute
functions.evidence:
Slot 6 of `CSetPlanForcesCommand` - the command's own **Execute** (see `CCommand::Execute`). It resolves its `unit` reference, hands the `min` vector it carries at `+0x64` to `CUnitPlan::SetMinForces` (`0x4DF0F0`), which replaces plan `+0x70` - `CUnit +0x26C`, already named `plan_subunit_wanted` - and then calls `CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds` so the shortfall per subunit type is recomputed against the new target.

The two calls to `RefreshPlanForceNeeds` (`0x1E8928` and `0x1E8934`) are the two arms of the second lookup, not two refreshes: the second passes `eax = 0`, the null arm of a resolve the compiler inlined twice. So it refreshes once, and would dereference null if the unit had gone - which `IsValid` prevents.
(reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

functions.name: ParseObjectReference
functions.evidence:
**Reads the `{ type = N id = N }` block a save writes for an object reference into the 0x28-byte reference a command keeps.** It calls `ParseObjectId` (0x67B250) for the pair and then fills the reference: `+0` the cached object pointer, set to 0 because the block names no object yet; `+4` type; `+8` id; `+0xC` an `Hoi3CString` assigned from the parse context's own name at `+0x32C`. It takes no stack argument - the parse context arrives in ECX and the reference in ESI (`mov ecx,[ebp+8]` and `lea esi,[this+0x3C]` at the call site, a bare `ret` here), the same register-argument style as the rest of the loader primitives. 61 call sites, every one of them a command's `LoadKey` case for a key whose value is an object: `unit` is token 0x256 and `parent` 0x84, and a command keeps one such reference per key at `+0x3C`, `+0x64` and so on, 0x28 apart. **It stores nothing when the parse context's error handler at `+0x35C` has latched** - handler non-null and both its bytes at `+4` and `+5` set jumps straight to the epilogue and leaves the reference as it was, although `ParseObjectId` has already consumed the tokens. The mirror image is the command's `SaveContents`, e.g. `CMoveCommand`'s at 0x1D9160: `SaveWriteKey(0x256)` then the pair out of `+0x40` and `+0x44` - the string at `+0x4C` is never written to the save. The same reference is built from a live object by 0x2DD70 (unnamed): type from `CUnit +0x10`, id from `+0x14`, the string from the object's `+0x1C`, and the object pointer cached at `+0`.
(reversing/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: LoadKey
functions.evidence:
**Only the dates.** The loader `CCountryHistory` and `CProvinceHistory` share: if the key is not a date it goes straight to **vftable slot 9**, the derived class's entry handler; if it is, the date is parsed and every key/value pair in the block that follows goes to slot 9 instead. So a dated block is nothing but a way of postponing the one grammar, which is why anything valid at the top of a country file is valid inside one. **Ghidra's analysis does not find this function** - only a vftable reaches it.
(BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountryHistory.hpp)

functions.name: AnnounceLoadedUnitsToScreen
functions.evidence:
**Tells the interface about a country's units**, which is the last thing CLoadOOBEffect::Execute does - and only when a scenario is running and the country is the **player's own**, so it is presentation rather than game state. It takes the thing at `CCountry + 0x1D8`, whose CCountryTag at `+0x20` gives it the country, walks that country's `units`, and for each one that passes a virtual test builds a 0x64 byte object and hands it to a virtual on `CCurrentGameState::in_game_screen`. **What `CCountry + 0x1D8` is has not been established**, nor which alert this raises. The name is BiceLib's.
(reversing/FINDINGS-effecttext.md)

functions.name: ComputePlanWantedSubUnits
functions.evidence:
Builds the order of battle a plan asks for. Called only from CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds (rva 0x1BD240), twice, and it is what fills CUnit::plan_subunit_wanted. In order: (1) grows `wanted` to GetNumberOfSubUnits() entries and zeroes every one of them (0x8E1DB3..0x8E1E39, the loop bound is (db+0x20 - db+0x1C)/4); (2) resolves about a dozen roles to concrete subunit types by taking the database's cached role definitions at db+0x2C, +0x34, +0x38, +0x3C, +0x40, +0x50, +0x58, +0x6C, +0x7C, +0x80 and +0x84 (those eleven and no others; 0x1ADF70 reaches six more of the same block, +0x44, +0x78, +0x98, +0xA0, +0xA8 and +0xAC) and keeping each only if the owner's availability byte array says so - `country->+0xDF8->+0x27C[definition->type_index] != 0` and then the second test at rva 0x1A3BC0 - falling back to db+0x34 otherwise (0x8E1E3F..0x8E2075); (3) collects the unit's own regiments through rva 0x1BD930 and accumulates, into *ownStrength, each one's strength (CRegiment +0x5C) over its maximum times its organisation over CSubUnit::GetMaxOrganisation, counting them by category with the 0..6 classifier at rva 0x1A8540 (0x8E20C4..0x8E22A2); (4) walks the plan's province list at [area], and for each province its 0x14-byte border records at +0xD4 ->+0x90..+0x94, skipping type 3, accumulating into *areaStrength (0x8E2387..0x8E26E0); (5) turns that frontage into counts using the plan type at plan+0xC (2, 3 and 4 each select a different global) and several defines, and finally does `wanted[definition->type_index]++` once per requested regiment for each role (0x8E2FE0, 0x8E3027, 0x8E31B6, 0x8E31E2). `useArea` switches the source of the scope: with it set the caller supplies `area` and the regiment collection is filtered by it; with it clear the unit's whole OOB is used and `area` is the plan's own province list. Returns nothing - eax is zero on every path and neither call site reads it.
(reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

functions.name: GetLeader
functions.evidence:
**The leader the effect names.** Its value sits at `+0x20` as a thousandth, so the id written in the event file is `value / 1000`, and that goes to the lookup at `0x69DA00` with the type 0x25. Answers null while the game has no leaders to look in. The compiler kept it to itself and passes the effect in **eax**. The name is BiceLib's.
(reversing/FINDINGS-effecttext.md)

functions.name: GetText
functions.evidence:
**The shape every effect's text builder has**, slot 9: it builds the sentence into `out`, answers it in eax, and takes forty bytes of arguments (`ret 0x28`). Of those the scope is read by 66 of the 99 effect classes that have a slot 9, and the string at `+0x10` by 75 - but only to destroy it, never to read its characters, so `unread` is what it is called here. The last eight bytes are read by none of the 99; they are written out so the stack adds up. This one names the localisation string `KILL_LEADER_EFFECT`, finds the leader in the scope country's active list and puts "\xa7Y<name>\xa7W" in place of its $NAME$. BiceLib stands in for two of its calls to add $UNIT$, $LOCATION$ and $WHERE$ - see Hooks/EffectText/KillLeaderText.cpp.
(reversing/FINDINGS-effecttext.md)

functions.name: Execute
functions.evidence:
Loads the order of battle the effect names: `CStringEffect::text` is written onto the country by CCountry::SetOobFile, and CCountry::LoadOobFile is called on it. The country is the scope's, by the id at `scope + 0x14`. **Nothing about the file is in memory before this**, which is why a tooltip about it has to read the file itself. The second stack argument is not read here; it is written out so the `ret 8` adds up. The name is BiceLib's.
(reversing/FINDINGS-effecttext.md)

functions.name: GetText
functions.evidence:
**The shape every effect's text builder has**, slot 9: it builds the sentence into `out`, answers it in eax, and takes forty bytes of arguments (`ret 0x28`). Of those the scope is read by 66 of the 99 effect classes that have a slot 9, and the string at `+0x10` by 75 - but only to destroy it, never to read its characters, so `unread` is what it is called here. The last eight bytes are read by none of the 99; they are written out so the stack adds up. This one hands **the effect's own string** - `CStringEffect::text`, which for this effect is the order of battle's path - to GetText as though it were a localisation key, so a player sees the bare path. There is no key and no variable to fill, so BiceLib writes the whole string over it at the last call before the return - see Hooks/EffectText/LoadOobText.cpp. **It is also a BiceLib patch site**: its first three instructions come to exactly five bytes, which is what a jump needs, and all the stub wants is ecx.
(reversing/FINDINGS-effecttext.md)

functions.name: fromCString
functions.evidence:
MSVC's `std::basic_string<char>::basic_string(const char*)`, statically linked and given a register calling convention by LTCG: the string is in ESI and the C string in EDX, nothing is on the stack, and `this` comes back in EAX. The body is the textbook two steps. First `_Tidy()` on an *uninitialised* object - `[esi+0x14] = 0xF` (_Myres), `[esi+0x10] = 0` (_Mysize), `[esi] = 0` (_Buf[0]), the same 0x18-byte layout `std::string::assign` at 0xA160 already reads. Then `assign(_Ptr, _Traits::length(_Ptr))`: a four-instruction inline strlen (`lea edi,[eax+1]` / `mov cl,[eax]; inc eax; test cl,cl; jne` / `sub eax,edi`) whose result is pushed with the pointer before `mov ecx,esi; call 0xA160`. **6732 direct call sites**, far more than any other unnamed function left, and it is how every loader, log line and error message turns a literal into a string - the caller is invariably `mov edx,<literal>; lea esi,<fresh local>; call`, followed by the EH state byte being stepped for the new object. There is no null check on EDX, which is what separates the constructor from an assignment.
(reversing/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: operatorPlus

functions.evidence:

functions.name: writeCString
functions.evidence:
**`os.write(text, strlen(text))` for a NUL-terminated string**, and the `<<` that 427 call sites use to put a C string into the game's log. `strlen` is open-coded as the four-instruction byte scan at `0xA64A10`; the length and a zero high dword are then pushed with the pointer and the stream and `std::ostream::write` (`0x664A30`) is called. It answers the stream in `eax` so the idiom chains: `LogRecord::Make(file, line, channel) << "text" << ... << endl`.

**The convention is one the optimiser invented, not `__cdecl` as written on a page.** Both arguments arrive in registers - the stream in `esi` (never saved, never reloaded: the epilogue is `mov eax, esi`) and the string in `edx` (`mov eax, edx` is the first thing the body does) - and the function ends in a bare `ret` having consumed nothing from the stack. `0x434389` is a plain example: `mov edx, 0x15B65D0 ('Bad messagetype'); mov esi, eax; call 0xA64A00; push eax; call std::endl`. This is the same re-signing that gave `std::string::fromCString` (`0x65A7A0`) its `this@ESI, text@EDX` and `std::ostream::flush` (`0x65BB20`) its `this@ESI`.

**It is not `std::operator<<Chars` (`0x21D30`), and the difference is real.** `0x21D30` is MSVC's `_Insert_string`: it reads `ios_base::_Wide` at `+0x20/+0x24`, computes the padding, emits `_Fillch` from `+0x40` and finishes with `width(0)`. This one does none of that - it goes straight to `write`, so a stream with a non-zero `width()` formats differently through the two. **What I could not settle** is whether that makes it a second `operator<<(ostream&, const char*)` from a translation unit built against a different `<ostream>`, or an engine-local unpadded fast inserter; the name records what it does rather than deciding that.

The four call sites that do not load `edx` from a string literal are the reason this wrapper exists at all: where the length is not a compile-time constant the compiler cannot fold it, so it calls the scanner instead of `write` directly.
(reversing/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: DestroyStringsInRange
functions.evidence:
**Empties the string at the start of every record in a range**, walking `[first, last)` in steps of **0x20** and giving each string's buffer back where it had one - `if (capacity >= 0x10) free(data)`, then capacity 0xF, length 0, first byte 0. Both ends arrive in registers, first in eax and last in edi. `ret`.

It is a destructor loop the compiler wrote once and **1552 call sites share**: every record type of 0x20 bytes that begins with a string folds onto this one body, which is why its callers have nothing to do with each other. The stride is baked in, so it is only correct for that shape.

BiceLib meets it tearing a text object down: after ReleaseTextReplacements has destroyed the object each replacement points at, this empties the name each one carries, and the caller frees the block. The name is BiceLib's.
(reversing/FINDINGS-effecttext.md)

functions.name: Write
functions.evidence:
**Where every message in the game arrives.** The record's destructor pulls the four apart and calls this through the sink's vftable slot 1. It opens with a filter of its own - `call 0x40C3C0` on a global at `0x16052F0`, taking the message and dropping it when that answers true - and only then picks a file by channel. **Measured, 2026-09-20**, by catching a whole startup: `3` writes to `system.log`, `0x10000` to `setup.log`, `0x10002` to `game.log`, `0x10006` to `time.log`, and every channel the run produced reached a file. `0x10004`, which carries the three `Unknown History Command` sites, was never produced at all. **Hooked once, on 2026-09-20**, with a five byte jump over the prologue (`55 8B EC 6A FF`) - ahead of the filter, so every message built was seen. That capture matched `setup.log` and `game.log` line for line, which is how the filter was shown to drop nothing, and the hook was then removed as redundant. `ret 0x10`.
(reversing/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: _Tidy
functions.evidence:
`ios_base::_Tidy()` - runs the registered callbacks with `erase_event` and then frees both of `ios_base`'s owned lists:

    _Callfns(erase_event);                 // 0x794AEE, with the literal 0
    for (p = _Arr;   p; p = next) free(p); _Arr = 0;      // +0x28
    for (p = _Calls; p; p = next) free(p); _Calls = 0;    // +0x2C

Both loops read the `_Next` pointer at offset `0` of the node before freeing it, which is the `_Iosarray` / `_Calls_t` layout. `__thiscall`, no stack arguments, bare `ret`. Recorded here because it is the only callee of `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor` that was not already named and it is what fixes `+0x28` and `+0x2C` as the two list heads.
(reversing/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: _Addstd
functions.evidence:
The increment side of the standard-stream reference count that `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor` (`0x794BAE`) decrements. Under `_Lockit(_LOCK_STREAM)` - the literal `2` passed to `0x79504A` - it scans the eight-entry pointer table at VA `0x174C818` from index 1 for a free slot or for itself, stores the index in `ios_base +8`, stores the pointer in the table and increments the byte at `0x174C840 + index`. `__cdecl`, one stack argument, bare `ret`.

Recorded here rather than left on the frontier because it is the evidence that `ios_base +8` is the standard-stream index and that the byte array at `0x174C840` is a refcount - without it the guard at the top of `0x794BAE` is unreadable.
(reversing/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: _Ios_base_dtor
functions.evidence:
**Confirmed: this is the `ios_base` destructor**, specifically the out-of-line static body that MSVC's `virtual ~ios_base()` consists of a single call to. The earlier report guessed right.

    if (_Stdstr == 0 || --_Stdstr_refs[_Stdstr] <= 0) {
        _Tidy();                                  // 0x794B15
        if (_Ploc) { _Ploc->~locale(); free(_Ploc); }
    }

The guard is the standard-stream reference count. `ios_base +8` is the slot index into an eight-entry table of standard streams at VA `0x174C818` with a parallel byte refcount array at VA `0x174C840`; this function decrements that byte and returns without tearing anything down while it is still positive, so `cout`/`cerr`/`clog` survive every `ios_base::Init` but the last. `std::ios_base::_Addstd` (`0x794B59`) is the only other code in the image that touches either table, and it increments exactly the byte this decrements.

When it does tear down: `_Tidy()` releases the `_Arr` and `_Calls` lists (`+0x28`, `+0x2C`), then `_Ploc` at `+0x30` gets `std::locale::~locale` (`0x2EE40`, `this` in `ecx`) followed by `free` (`0x795F9B`, which is what `operator delete` folded to here).

**How the 700 call sites read.** Every one of them is a derived class destroying its `ios_base` base, and each writes the `ios_base` virtual table `0x15A7B8C` into the object immediately before the call - textbook base-subobject destruction with the vfptr reset. `LogRecord::Flush` (`0x24B0`) is the example the handover named:

    lea esi, [eax+0x78]          ; the ios_base subobject inside the record
    push esi; call LogRecord::FlushAndDestruct
    push esi; mov [esi], 0x15A7B8C
    call 0x794BAE

`__cdecl`, one stack argument at `[ebp+8]`, bare `ret`, no return value. It is *not* itself virtual and sits in no class's virtual table; the virtual destructor that calls it is the scalar deleting destructor at `0x2210`, which is unnamed and left for the next wave.
(reversing/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: operator_new
functions.evidence:
**`operator new`, and so every allocation the game's own code makes.** Ghidra calls it `FUN_00b9602f`, and it is the function behind a `push <size>` / `call` pair - `push 0xB0` before a log record, `push 0x57C` before a country database. The size is the object's, which makes a call site worth reading: it is how big the thing about to be built is.

The standard MSVC body, a retry loop: call `malloc` (`0x796CC3`); on success return it; on failure call `_callnewh` (`0x79F4F7`) to give the new handler a chance to free something and try again; when the handler answers 0, **throw `std::bad_alloc`** - its vftable is `0x119FCE8` - through `_CxxThrowException` (`0x79894B`). So it never returns null.

The `mov edi, edi` it opens with is the two byte hot patch pad, which is why the body starts at `+2`.
(reversing/FINDINGS-allocator.md)

functions.name: _purecall
functions.evidence:
The CRT stub a class's own vftable holds for a method it leaves pure virtual - COrder's slot 16, the order type id, among many. It calls the installed _purecall_handler if there is one and otherwise ends the process through _amsg_exit(_RT_PUREVIRT), the R6025 "pure virtual function call" message, so reaching it is fatal. Nothing reaches it in a working game: every concrete class fills the slot. Three Lua registrations resolve here - CCommand::IsValid, CDiplomaticAction::IsValid and CDiplomaticAction::GetAIAcceptance - because those methods are pure virtual in the class that declares them; the findings used to name this address after them (Shared_GetAIAcceptance_IsValid) and no longer do.

**Read out in full**, because it is where a crash can be caught: `push [__pPurecall]` (`0x134D238`, kept encoded), `call [DecodePointer]`, `test eax,eax`, `je` past it, `call eax` with no arguments - and then `push 0x19`, **25 = `_RT_PUREVIRT`**, which is what identifies this function rather than one of the other handler wrappers in this CRT that also decode a pointer and call it.

**510 slots in the data sections hold this address and nothing calls it directly.** The game installs no handler, so reaching it is fatal as the comment above says; BiceLib installs one and saves the game before it goes - GameState/PureCall.cpp and reversing/FINDINGS-allocator.md.
(reversing/CLASSES.md:347)

Rejects a null string or a null format with errno=EINVAL (0x16) and _invalid_parameter_noinfo, then fakes a FILE on its stack over the string - _flag 0x49, _ptr=_base=string, _cnt=min(strlen(string), INT_MAX) - and tail-calls the INPUTFN it was handed. functions.name: sscanf
functions.evidence:
MSVC CRT `sscanf`, statically linked. The body is only the public wrapper: it loads the buffer into esi and calls the file-scope helper at 0x796466 with (INPUTFN=_input_l 0x7A1379, format, locale=NULL, va_list=&arg3), which builds a FILE on its own stack over the string (_flag=0x49 = _IOREAD|_IOMYBUF|_IOSTRG, _ptr=_base=buffer, _cnt=min(strlen(buffer), INT_MAX)) and runs the scan engine over it. **This is the single most-called unnamed function in the image, 168 direct call sites**, and it is how every loader turns a lexed token into a number: 152 of those sites push exactly three arguments and clean 0xc, with the middle one a literal format - `%i` 102 times, `%f` 28, `%u` 18, `%c` 8, and one each of `%x`, `%lld` and `%d.%d.%d.%d` - and the return is tested against zero, which is sscanf's count of fields assigned. The string argument is almost always `parse + 0x22C`, the lexer's current token text.
(reversing/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: __alldiv
functions.evidence:
MSVC CRT signed 64-bit divide (lldiv.asm). Dividend at [esp+4..0xB], divisor at [esp+0xC..0x13]; result in edx:eax; callee cleans 16 bytes (ret 0x10). Truncates toward zero, NOT floor: it takes the absolute value of both operands, divides unsigned, and negates the quotient only if exactly one operand was negative (edi counts the negations at 0xB9998D and 0xB999A9, and 0xB99A1A negates when edi==1). 2032 direct call sites. This is the helper every 'x * 1000 / y' in the game goes through - the thousandths fixed point multiplies into a 64-bit intermediate to avoid overflow and then divides here.
(reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

functions.name: __allrem
functions.evidence:
MSVC CRT signed 64-bit remainder (llrem.asm). With the two saved registers on the stack the dividend is at [esp+0xC..0x13] and the divisor at [esp+0x14..0x1B]; remainder in edx:eax; callee cleans 16 bytes (ret 0x10). **The remainder takes the dividend's sign alone**, which is what tells it apart from __alldiv at 0x799980: the two bodies are otherwise the same shape, but __alldiv has `inc edi` on both the dividend branch (0xB9998D) and the divisor branch (0xB999A9) and negates when exactly one operand was negative, while this one has `inc edi` on the dividend branch (0xB99A3C) and **none** on the divisor branch at 0xB99A56, so the flag counts only the dividend - and the tail tests it with `jns` rather than __alldiv's `jne`. It is signed, not __aullrem, which has no sign handling at all. 7 direct call sites.
(reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

functions.name: __allmul
functions.evidence:
MSVC CRT 64-bit multiply (llmul.asm). a at [esp+4..0xB], b at [esp+0xC..0x13]; result in edx:eax; callee cleans 16 bytes (ret 0x10). Sign-agnostic: the low 64 bits of the product are the same for signed and unsigned operands, so MSVC emits this one body for both, and the sign lives at the CALL SITE - a 'cdq' before the push means the 32-bit operand was signed, a 'xor edx,edx' means it was not. Fast path when both high words are zero (0xB99B00, a single mul), otherwise the three partial products AHI*BLO + ALO*BHI + ALO*BLO. 1144 direct call sites.
(reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

functions.name: __allshl
functions.evidence:
MSVC CRT 64-bit left shift (llshl.asm). Value in edx:eax, count in cl, result in edx:eax, nothing on the stack, bare ret. Three cases: count >= 64 answers zero (0xB99B4A), count >= 32 moves eax into edx and shifts it by count&31 with eax zeroed (0xB99B40), otherwise `shld edx, eax, cl` then `shl eax, cl` (0xB99B3A). Sign-agnostic - a left shift is the same body for signed and unsigned, which is why MSVC emits one body for both. 4 direct call sites.
(reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

labels.name: __pPurecall
labels.evidence:
The pure virtual call handler, kept **encoded** with `EncodePointer` - so it cannot be read out of memory as a pointer, and a decode of null is what says none is installed.

labels.name: g_CSubUnitDataBase
labels.evidence:
The one CSubUnitDataBase, 0xC0 bytes, built lazily: every user does `if (!g_CSubUnitDataBase) CSubUnitDataBase::SetInstance(new CSubUnitDataBase)`. Layout as the constructor at rva 0x1ADEE0 and the four Lua accessors show it - +0x00..+0x0B a three-dword container zeroed at construction; +0x10..+0x1B a name -> definition hash map (count at +0x10, 0x1FF buckets at +0x14, the bucket array allocated at +0x18), which GetSubUnit searches; +0x1C..+0x27 a CArray<CSubUnitDefinition*> (begin/end/capacity), which GetSubUnitList returns by reference and GetSubUnitByIndex indexes, so the element stride is 4 and the entry count is (+0x20 - +0x1C)/4; +0x28..+0xAC a block of cached CSubUnitDefinition* for well-known roles, left uninitialised by the constructor and filled at load time; +0xB0..+0xBB a second three-dword container. The count at (+0x20 - +0x1C)/4 is what sizes every array indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index, CUnit::plan_subunit_wanted among them.
(reversing/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

labels.name: Define10
labels.evidence:
A define, 10 - the floor of the float 10.5, taken at startup. Thousandths, so 0.010. Ten places read it and they do not agree on a purpose, so the name only says what it holds. CUnit's supply and fuel consumption (0x1BB560, 0x1BB7A0) add `CRegiment +0xCC x this` to a potency whose base is 1000, so each point of that field is 1% more consumption. Elsewhere it is a floor on a multiplier (0x1C30B6 clamps 1000 + x up to it before scaling max_strength), a threshold (0x1C638A) and an additive base (0x1CDA8C). Which define it is has not been established.
(reversing/CLASSES.md:267)

labels.name: Define50
labels.evidence:
A define, 50 - the floor of the float 50.5, taken at startup. Thousandths, so 0.050. Five places read it and they do not agree on a purpose. CUnit's supply and fuel consumption multiply the army group leader's skill (CLeader +0x70) by it, scaled by how far that HQ's command reaches; the other three compare it against a unit's supply_received_percentage (+0xFC) and fuel_received_percentage (+0x100) to flag a unit that is short. 0x16886E8 is a separate global holding the same value from the same float. One name for it fits the consumption use and not the other three; which define it is has not been established.
(reversing/CLASSES.md:267)

labels.name: CLeader_AddExperience_rankFactor
labels.evidence:
**A function-local static inside CLeader::AddExperience**, not a global anyone else uses: five 64-bit fixed points indexed by the leader's rank, behind the one-byte construction guard at 0x17EB710. The constructor fills all five from the double 32768.5 at 0x120A548, truncated to 32768 - exactly 1.0 - so **rank does not change how fast a leader learns**. **Read live**: all five are 32768 and the guard is 1, and the whole image references the array only from the ten writes that fill it and the two reads that index it.
(BiceLib/GameClasses/CLeader.hpp:113)

labels.name: CLeader_AddExperience_rankFactorBuilt
labels.evidence:
The one-byte guard MSVC puts in front of a function-local static: `test byte ptr [this], 1; jne skip` at the top, `or [this], 1` before the constructor runs. Its presence is what tells you the addresses beside it are a local static rather than a global.
(BiceLib/GameClasses/CLeader.hpp:113)
